interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary: Scotland’s power network is currently demonstrating exceptional renewable performance, anchored by a robust 4.4 GW of wind generation. This substantial green volume has suppressed regional carbon intensity to a low 32 gCO2/kWh, reinforcing Scotland’s critical role as the clean energy backbone of Great Britain. However, this generation surge also exposes persistent structural frictions within the wider transmission architecture. Telemetry registers 221.1 MWh of wasted energy through curtailment, illustrating acute capacity bottlenecks across key transfer corridors, most notably the B6 Anglo-Scottish boundary. While local demand and cross-border interconnector links absorb the vast majority of clean generation, shedding zero-marginal-cost power represents a clear economic and operational challenge for system operators. To mitigate these constraint costs and maximize asset utilization, strategic investments must accelerate the deployment of co-located battery storage, synchronous condensers, and flexible industrial demand-side response. In the immediate term, current metrics depict an environmentally optimal grid running predominantly on low-carbon electrons; yet, unlocking Scotland's full generation potential sustainably requires rapid reinforcement of transmission headroom to balance regional surplus with broader national demand.
